rationale: oopack_v1p8 is a small (3.2 KB text, 26 functions) C++ benchmark whose hot code is tight numeric loops (mandelbrot, big-fibonacci, container iteration in Benchmark::time_one/time_both), so runtime overhead is the binding constraint: cheap, semantics-preserving passes are favored while expensive control-flow passes are dampened. SUB and SPLIT get high weights across the board because they add static diversity at near-zero runtime and size cost and carry minimal correctness risk on straightforward C++ code. FLA keeps a strong SecurityGain since flattening the few medium-sized functions (main, time_both, time_one) yields the largest single analysis hurdle, but its RuntimeCost weight is pulled down to 0.3 so flattening concentrates only on loop-light functions rather than the hot inner loops. BCF is dampened hardest (RuntimeCost/SizeCost 0.2) because bogus branches inside mandel/fib iteration loops would inflate both runtime and text size disproportionately for a 3 KB binary; its residual weight lets it trigger only on cold wrapper functions whose features favor security. IBR gets a mild profile (indirect branches hinder static CFG recovery at moderate cost), while ICALL is held near neutral-low: this code is template/vtable-heavy C++, so aggressive indirect-call rewriting risks breaking calls through virtual dispatch and member-function pointers, hence CorrectnessRisk 0.5 and RuntimeCost 0.3. IGV is kept moderately low because with only 26 functions and a small module, inter-procedural value-hiding adds little resistance relative to its size cost. Overall the table biases selection toward SUB+SPLIT everywhere, FLA on non-loop-heavy functions, and only opportunistic BCF/ICALL/IGV on cold code.
